$comment: Public-repository leak check (scripts/security/public-denylist.mjs). Generic rules only: they name no installation and no person. A maintainer's own domains, addresses, hosts, names and private paths go in a private list outside the repository (--extra), never here and never hashed: a hash of a short value is cheap to brute-force. Every allow / except entry needs a reason. Rules are evaluated in order and a line reports each category once, so the more specific rule of a category comes first.

allow.reason: the denylist itself: rule patterns and allowlist globs name what they forbid

topLevel.reason: a new top-level directory or root file is a public-surface decision: add it here deliberately

rules.$comment: 123456789012 is the AWS documentation account id
the default host name of an EC2 instance names its private address; docs and tests use synthetic names

except.reason: obviously synthetic sample host names used by tests and examples (first addresses of a range, documentation ranges)

rules.$comment: an ssh command with an explicit key file under ~/.ssh names a key file and usually a host; docs use <key> / <host>
warning only, and only where host addresses live: version strings such as 2.56.0.3 look like addresses

except.reason: Cloudflare's published edge ranges (cloudflare.com/ips) as the default trusted proxy sources of the Coolify proxy
a four-part Git for Windows (MinGit) version number, not an address

rules.$comment: a real home directory names a person; generic names (alex, user, runner, ubuntu, one- or two-letter names, system folders, the product's own service accounts) are placeholders

Library/Application Support is the standard macOS location of the product's own worker directories (RemyralWorker, legacy RemanaWorker, remyral-worker) and of the browser / password-manager profiles the macOS sandbox denies (apps/worker/src/sandbox/host/seatbelt.ts); any other application directory there is someone's local tooling
the generated default name of a Windows machine

allow.reason: applied migration, never edited (checksummed by the migrator): its header comment cites a historical update rollback
vendored Node.js release signing keys: the OpenPGP user ids carry the releasers' public addresses

rules.$comment: history mode: an author / committer address git made up from the local user and machine name (user.email unset). Contributors' real addresses are theirs to publish and pass; a maintainer's own addresses belong in the private list.
